gapClosure.executive_summary: All four gating gaps the completeness critic raised are now closed with measured data, and every signal points GO for the from-scratch Rust Luau interpreter. (1) PERF: on grabby's REAL integer-AI kernel (not the string-sort bench the old 4x came from), reference Luau via mlua measures 0.73 us/decision apples-to-apples with koto's path = 8.1x faster than koto-int (5.9) and 6.0x faster than koto-float (4.4) on the same aarch64-mac, comfortably under the 1.0-1.25 us target; even running the ENTIRE loop in-script is 1.45 us = 4.1x over koto. This validates the register-bytecode-VM approach as the performance BAR (rustia must hit it; it does not inherit it). (2) WASM GATE: the feared ~4x wasm dispatch tax is refuted - a match->br_table loop runs at 0.85-1.10x of native in V8 (node V8 actually FASTER than native), so in-browser viability reduces to native per-decision cost. (3) T1: f64 + the pure-Rust libm crate + NaN/signed-zero canonicalization + no-FMA is bit-identical across x86_64-linux, aarch64-mac AND wasm32 (combined hash 0x4fcaf33760ef5a9a on all three; raw/uncanonicalized diverges) - resolving the f64-vs-fixed-point tension WITHOUT adding a fixed-point primitive to the core Value. (4) Send-vs-Sync: grabby never shares a &VM across threads (sim App is !Send/NonSend-pinned, real threads run separate worlds via mpsc), so only Send is required - Sync is over-engineering. Embedding the real Luau C++ to wasm is dead: it will not compile to wasm32-unknown-unknown at all (no C++ stdlib; 'iterator' not found on the first file) and the emscripten escape hatch cannot compose with grabby's wasm-bindgen Bevy module. A samply profile of koto-int shows its cost is 29% bytecode-decode (Iterator-based reader), ~20% KValue Arc clone+drop, ~8% range-iterator - directly prescribing rustia's levers: tight match dispatch + superinstructions, Copy-scalar/traced-heap value layout (no Arc refcount on the hot path), and dedicated numeric-for opcodes. MVP Luau scope is ~70 opcodes + 5 core libs + coroutine + Lua-5.1 patterns + Schubfach tostring + pure-Rust libm. The one number still entirely TBD is rustia's OWN us/decision - that is the next spike.

### WASM dispatch tax (ns/dispatch, best-of-5; Spike B)
| Dispatch style | native (aarch64) | node V8 25.8 | deno V8 14.9 | wasm tax |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **match -> br_table** (recommended) | 1.217 | 1.028 | 1.338 | **0.85x-1.10x (~parity)** |
| fnptr / call-threaded (call_indirect) | 2.234 | 2.995 | 3.361 | 1.34x-1.51x |
Native fnptr/match = 1.84x (indirect calls block inlining). checksum=800000000 bit-identical across native/node/deno. Conclusion: one portable big-match core is optimal on BOTH targets; no native/wasm dispatch split needed.

### libm bit-identity (FNV-1a combined hash over 46-value sweep; Spike C)
| Target | combined_canon (libm crate + NaN/signed-zero canon) | combined_raw (no canon) |

| aarch64-mac | 0x4fcaf33760ef5a9a | 0x0c87e93abd96c30a |

gapClosure.wasm_gate_verdict: GO. The feared ~4x wasm dispatch tax is decisively refuted (Spike B). For the match->br_table dispatch style rustia should ship, wasm-in-V8 runs at 0.85x-1.10x of native ns/dispatch - essentially parity, with node V8 (1.028 ns) actually FASTER than the native build (1.217 ns) and deno (1.338 ns) only 1.10x. Measured tax multiplier = 0.85x-1.10x (call it ~1.0x). Therefore the dispatch+ALU core imposes ~zero wasm penalty: whatever per-decision cost rustia achieves natively, in-browser it is ~1.0-1.3x of that, dominated by native instruction count, not a wasm tax. The browser-viability question reduces to native per-decision cost (still TBD, next spike). Two corollaries: (a) NO native/wasm dispatch split is needed - the landscape doc's 'tail-call on native, match on wasm' hypothesis is overturned; function-pointer/call-threading is strictly worse on BOTH targets (1.84x slower than match natively, 1.34-1.51x wasm tax from call_indirect bounds+type checks); ship one big-match core everywhere, computed-goto/CPS is unnecessary because plain br_table is already at native parity in V8. (b) JIT-to-native is correctly a native-only stretch tier, not the browser path. CONDITIONS/CAVEATS bounding the GO: measured only on an aarch64-mac host's V8 (node/deno) - x86_64-linux and mobile-ARM V8, plus JSC/SpiderMonkey, are unmeasured; it is a microbench of dispatch + integer/Q16.16 ALU only - a full VM adds linear-memory bounds checks, table/string/heap loads, GC, and call_indirect for closures/host calls that could stress wasm differently; and it proves the wasm/native RATIO, not absolute fit to the 5ms budget. None of these threaten the gate (the ~4x killer was the only NO-GO trigger and it is gone), but the full-VM wasm ratio must be re-confirmed in the rustia walking-skeleton spike.

resolved_tensions.tension: T1 - Luau f64-only vs grabby's i64/Q16.16 float-free determinism boundary (the pivotal tension)
resolved_tensions.resolution: RESOLVED in rustia's favor: f64-internal, NO fixed-point primitive in the core Value type. Adopt f64 + the pure-Rust libm crate for ALL transcendentals + NaN-payload/sign and signed-zero canonicalization + no-FMA/no-fast-math. Offer the Luau `buffer` library (little-endian, exact i8..i64 read/write) as the secondary deterministic integer/serialization channel, and keep grabby's Q16.16 multiply as a host fn (zero new VM work). The experimental int64 LUA_TINTEGER lib is a deferrable opt-in, not a compat requirement.
resolved_tensions.evidence: Lang-spec: every Luau arithmetic opcode fast-paths on f64+vector ONLY (lvmexecute.cpp:1752); int64 exists in 0.727 but is FFlag-gated OFF (LuauIntegerLibrary=false), library-only, not wired to operators. grabby's hot path keeps Q16.16 multiply in host Rust and only does integer-valued control flow where every script-visible integer is <2^53 (exact in f64). Spike C PROVES the residual risk closed: f64 + libm crate + canonicalization yields combined hash 0x4fcaf33760ef5a9a bit-identical across x86_64-linux, aarch64-mac, AND wasm32; the only divergence (raw) is NaN sign/payload (sqrt(-1) = 0x7ff8... vs 0xfff8... on x86_64), neutralized by canonicalization.

resolved_tensions.tension: Send vs Sync at VM granularity (gc-arena collides with N-Send+Sync-VMs?)
resolved_tensions.resolution: RESOLVED: only SEND is required for the VM/values; SYNC is needed only for shared IMMUTABLE artifacts (compiled bytecode, LUTs, string interner) behind Arc. Do not pay for interior synchronization on the VM's mutable execution state. This directly de-risks gc-arena (you move whole arenas, never share Gc pointers across threads).
resolved_tensions.evidence: grabby-send-sync topology: no code anywhere shares a single &VM across threads. The sim App is !Send and stored as a Bevy NonSend resource that pins every tick to one thread (view/src/lib.rs:68-71); the console Koto VM is !Send/NonSend (console.rs:296); the only real threads run SEPARATE worlds communicating via mpsc channels (net/src/bin/server.rs:59, netclient.rs:70/151). No rayon/par_iter/thread::scope over VMs. The probe asserts only KValue: Send+Sync. 'N independent VMs across a thread pool' = own-and-move per thread = Send.

resolved_tensions.tension: gc-arena viability (ideal safe GC, but reputed not-Send/Sync and ergonomically heavy)
resolved_tensions.resolution: CONDITIONALLY VIABLE and now the leading GC direction. Adopt gc-arena's ARCHITECTURE (incremental tracing + the mutate-XOR-collect invariant that forces the stackless/steppable VM C3 wants) and collect at deterministic fuel boundaries. Keep per-agent AI hot/rollback state OUT of the GC heap, in host-side columnar Rust arrays, so it rides grabby's 24-deep no-serde ring with <=1ms restore. Gate adoption on a 1-day micro-spike verifying Arena: Send + serde-bridge + steppable ergonomics under the branded 'gc lifetime.
resolved_tensions.evidence: Send-only requirement (above) removes the primary objection - you move whole arenas, never share Gc across threads. Spike D quantifies the alternative's cost: ~20% of koto's self-time is KValue Arc clone+drop (refcounting), direct evidence FAVORING a tracing GC over Rc/Arc. Lang-spec: Luau has NO __gc finalizers (one fewer determinism hazard than Lua 5.4) and weak tables can be cleared at deterministic collection points. piccolo demonstrates gc-arena supports fuel + stackless steppable coroutines. Residual risk: gc-arena Arena: Send and branded-lifetime ergonomics vs the serde/embedding API are not yet prototyped (no direct spike).

resolved_tensions.tension: Embed/fork Luau-C++-compiled-to-wasm vs build-from-scratch (the alternative that could obviate the project)
resolved_tensions.resolution: RESOLVED decisively for from-scratch. Embedding the real Luau C++ VM is NON-VIABLE for grabby's shipping target and does not obviate rustia; it VALIDATES the from-scratch decision. Keep Luau C++ only as a technique/compat reference (interrupt-hook fuel model, register-VM encoding, GETIMPORT/FASTCALL inline caches), not a dependency.
resolved_tensions.evidence: Locally reproduced: mlua+Luau (vendored, Luau 0.663/0.709) builds and runs fine NATIVELY, but `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` FAILS on the first C++ file - 'Ast.h:6:10: fatal error: iterator file not found' - because wasm32-unknown-unknown ships no C++ stdlib/libc (more fundamental than the known setjmp issue). The only working path (emscripten/wasi) produces a different-ABI module with its own libc/malloc/JS-glue that CANNOT link into or compose with grabby's wasm32-unknown-unknown + wasm-bindgen Bevy module; the alternatives (separate Web Worker, or recompiling all of Bevy to emscripten) break the deterministic in-process 10k-decision/20ms tick or are unsupported. Plus meeting determinism would require a permanent invasive C++ fork (ltable.cpp iteration order + lmathlib.cpp libm + FMA flags), forfeiting the only benefit (free upstream compat). A pure-Rust VM compiles clean to wasm32-unknown-unknown and composes natively - the exact property Luau-C++ cannot provide.

gapClosure.language_scope:
MINIMUM-VIABLE LUAU SUBSET for grabby (scenarios + console + AI leaves), per the lang-spec scope triage.

OPCODES (~70 of Luau's 90): rustia OWNS its compiler+bytecode (not consuming Luau LBC v7), enabling superinstructions and dropping the ~8 Roblox-specific opcodes (GETUDATAKS/SETUDATAKS/NAMECALLUDATA/NEWCLASSMEMBER/CALLFB/CMPPROTO + class system) and lowering the 5 FASTCALL* to ordinary CALL; typeinfo/native-codegen bytecode ignored.

SYNTAX (parse+run): local/global vars; numeric AND generic for; while/repeat; if/elseif/else; functions+closures+varargs; table/array/map literals; indexing; all arithmetic/comparison/concat/logical operators; method calls (a:m()/a.m()); string literals; return/break. Plus cheap Luau niceties that scenarios/console use: continue, compound assignment (+= -= *= /= //= %= ^= ..=), floor-division //, number literals (0x/0b/1_000), string interpolation, generalized iteration (for v in t via __iter), if-then-else expressions. CRITICAL: the parser must ACCEPT-AND-IGNORE the full Luau type grammar (annotations, generics, type functions, @native/@checked attributes, default args) - types are runtime-erased, so a parser that ignores them suffices; the gradual type CHECKER (Luau Analysis/) is a separable, large, DEFERRABLE subsystem (only needed for editor/LSP diagnostics, not for running grabby).

LIBS (5 core + coroutine + base globals): math (incl. the pure-Rust libm transcendental set sin/cos/tan/asin/acos/atan/atan2/sinh/cosh/tanh/exp/log/log10/pow/fmod + Perlin math.noise table; sqrt is IEEE-safe; galaxy.koto DOES use .cos()/.sin()); table (insert/remove/sort[exact unstable introsort for tie-parity]/concat/find/clear/freeze/clone); string (format[pure-Rust float formatter, NOT platform snprintf]/find/match/gsub/sub/rep/split + full Lua-5.1 pattern engine); bit32 (15 fns, deterministic, no libm); buffer (~28 methods, little-endian-normalized, the exact-integer/serialization + serde channel). coroutine (create/resume/yield/wrap/status/close/isyieldable - the steppable host-integration surface). ~26 base globals: assert/error/print/type/typeof/tostring[exact Schubfach port for byte-parity]/tonumber/pairs/ipairs/next/select/pcall/xpcall/setmetatable/getmetatable/raw*/require/_G/_VERSION. 21 fast metamethods + __tostring (incl. Luau-specific __namecall/__iter/__type; NO __le-from-__lt synthesis; NO __gc). Sandbox: table.freeze/readonly + safeenv.

DETERMINISM OVERRIDES baked into the subset: math.random = exact PCG32 (mult 6364136223846793005, PCG-XSH-RR, Lemire range map) with a FORCED explicit seed (never Luau's time^clock^pointer default); os.time/clock/date virtualized behind a deterministic clock; maps are INSERTION-ORDERED (stricter than Luau's hash-bucket pairs() order - an accepted, documented incompatibility for hash/sparse keys; array-part 1..n matches); NaN rejected as table key; NaN/inf rendered via Schubfach not snprintf.

DEFER (full Roblox compat, not needed for grabby): vector type, utf8, string.pack, int64/LUA_TINTEGER lib, user-defined class runtime (LUA_TCLASS/TOBJECT), native codegen, the gradual type checker.

Treat the source as ground truth; treat luau.org Library/Syntax pages as the stable documented subset. Bytecode: LBC_VERSION_MIN=3, MAX=11, TARGET=7; typeinfo LBC_TYPE_VERSION_MIN=1, MAX=3, TARGET=3 (Common/include/Luau/Bytecode.h:501-507).

findings.topic: NUMBER MODEL — f64 is the only arithmetic type; resolves grabby tension T1
findings.finding: All arithmetic opcodes are f64-only. LOP_ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/MOD/POW/IDIV fast paths test ttisnumber (double) + ttisvector ONLY (VM/src/lvmexecute.cpp:1752 `setnvalue(ra, nvalue(rb)+nvalue(rc))`). lua_Number is double (luaconf.h). There is NO LUA_TINTEGER in any arithmetic path. HOWEVER 0.727 DOES define a real LUA_TINTEGER value tag (VM/include/lua.h:77) carrying int64, with a full `int` library (VM/src/lintlib.cpp: int.create/add/sub/mul/div/idiv/mod/udiv/urem/band/bor/bxor/bnot/lshift/rshift/arshift/lrotate/rrotate/extract/replace/lt/le/ult/min/max/clamp/countlz/countrz/bswap/fromstring/tonumber + int.maxsigned/minsigned, ~40 fns). CRITICAL: this is FFlag-gated by LuauIntegerLibrary which defaults to FALSE (Common/Common.h:137 LUAU_FASTFLAGVARIABLE(...,false,false)); linit.cpp:45 falls back to lualibs_NOINTEGER when off. int64 is NOT wired to operators — only to library functions and to EQ/NE opcodes (lvmexecute.cpp:1452,1585 pointer-style lvalue compare). So `a+b` on two int64 does NOT work; you must call int.add. Conclusion: int64 is a future opt-in carrier+library, exactly like bit32-for-64-bit, NOT a language-visible integer subtype.

findings.topic: T1 resolution guidance from grabby's actual hot path
findings.finding: grabby's AI script (ai_bakeoff/src/koto_path.rs SCRIPT) keeps ALL Q16.16 multiply in HOST fns (fxmul, curve); the script only does integer-valued control flow: numeric for 0..6 / 0..4, %, comparison, tuple index, assignment, constants ONE=65536/MOMENTUM=81920. Every script-visible integer is <2^53, where f64 represents integers and +,-,*,%,<,==,floor exactly. The ONLY op that breaks f64 is the 64-bit intermediate of a Q16.16 multiply (needs >>16 of a 64-bit product) — which grabby already keeps in Rust. So Luau's f64-only model is SUFFICIENT for grabby's control flow; the fixed-point multiply channel options for rustia are, in order of fit: (1) host native fn (what grabby does today, zero new VM work); (2) the `buffer` library (writei32/readinteger give exact 8/16/32/64-bit little-endian integer storage — see buffer finding); (3) bit32 for 32-bit; (4) adopt the experimental int64 lib later. Do NOT need to add a fixed-point primitive to the core value type for Luau-compat.

findings.topic: TABLE ITERATION ORDER — the central determinism delta
findings.finding: Luau next()/pairs() order (VM/src/ltable.cpp:224 luaH_next): (1) ARRAY part indices 1..sizearray in ascending numeric order; then (2) HASH part in PHYSICAL NODE-SLOT order (for i in 0..sizenode: emit non-nil nodes). Node slot = mainposition(key) = hash(key) mod sizenode (power-of-2), with collision chaining via getfreepos. This is HASH-BUCKET order, NOT insertion order. It IS deterministic across runs/platforms because the string hash is UNSEEDED and fixed (VM/src/lstring.cpp:10 luaS_hash = LuaJIT/lookup3 ARX for >=32-byte prefix + Lua-5.1 hash for short strings; constant, no per-state random seed; explicitly 'replicated in BytecodeBuilder::getStringHash'). BUT it depends on table capacity (rehash timing), insertion/deletion history, and key hash values. grabby REQUIRES insertion-ordered maps (C1). => rustia's insertion-order is a STRICTER, portable guarantee that will DIFFER from reference-Luau pairs() order on string/sparse-int-keyed tables. This is acceptable (no sane code depends on Luau bucket order, and rustia order is more deterministic), but rustia is NOT bit-compatible with Luau on pairs() traversal of hash-part keys — must be documented. Array-part order (sequential 1..n) DOES match.

VM/src/lmathlib.cpp:24 pcg32_random: state' = state*6364136223846793005 + (PCG32_INC|1); output = rotate-right of ((state>>18)^state)>>27 by (state>>59) (PCG-XSH-RR 64/32). Seeding (pcg32_seed): state=0; step; state+=seed; step. math.randomseed takes a 32-bit int. math.random(): two pcg32 draws → ldexp(rl|(rh<<32), -64) for [0,1). math.random(u): Lemire multiply-shift `1 + (u*pcg32()>>32)` (NOT modulo). math.random(l,u): `l + ((u-l+1)*pcg32()>>32)`. Default unseeded state mixes time(NULL)^clock()^pointer — NONDETERMINISTIC unless randomseed is called. rustia must (a) replicate PCG32 exactly bit-for-bit, (b) force an explicit deterministic seed (never the time/pointer default), (c) replicate the ldexp/multiply-shift range mapping exactly. RNG state lives in global_State (per-VM), which fits the N-independent-VMs model.

findings.topic: FLOAT FORMATTING — split between deterministic Schubfach and NON-portable snprintf
findings.finding: tostring(number) and number→string coercion use VM/src/lnumprint.cpp luai_num2str = SCHUBFACH (Raffaello Giulietti 2021), shortest round-trippable decimal, fully custom/deterministic; nan/inf rendered as fixed strings. BUT string.format with %e/%E/%f/%g/%G/%a routes through the PLATFORM snprintf (VM/src/lstrlib.cpp:1039 `snprintf(buff,sizeof(buff),form,(double)...)`), as do %d/%i/%u/%x via integer snprintf. Platform snprintf is NOT bit-identical across libc/targets (rounding, nan spelling like 'nan' vs '-nan(ind)', %a digits). => DETERMINISM HAZARD: reference Luau's own string.format is not cross-platform-deterministic. rustia MUST implement its own pure-Rust %e/%f/%g formatter (single impl for x86_64/aarch64/wasm32) and accept that its string.format output may diverge from a given platform's reference-Luau. tostring(number) should port Luau's exact Schubfach (note: Rust's ryu/grisu produce shortest round-trip too but tie-breaking/format differs, so a literal Schubfach port is needed for tostring byte-parity).

VM/src/ltablib.cpp:404 sort_rec = introsort: median-of-3 pivot (sorts a[l],a[m],a[u], pivot parked at u-1), Hoare partition, recurse smaller half + loop larger; recursion budget `limit` starts ~1.5*log2(n) and decays `limit=(limit>>1)+(limit>>2)`; on exhaustion falls back to sort_heap (binary heapsort). NOT stable. Detects bad comparators: 'invalid order function for sorting' and 'table modified during sorting'. => For a strict-total-order comparator any correct sort matches, but to be BIT-IDENTICAL with Luau when the comparator has ties (equal keys), rustia must replicate this exact pivot/partition/heapsort-fallback sequence (unstable order of equal elements is algorithm-defined). Default sort (no comparator) uses luaV_lessthan (numbers/strings).

findings.topic: VECTOR native type — f32 components, default 3-wide, operator-enabled
findings.finding: LUA_TVECTOR is a value type (not GC). Components are FLOAT (f32): TValue stores v[0],v[1] in the value union + v[2] in TValue::extra (lobject.h:39). LUA_VECTOR_SIZE default 3 (luaconf.h:137, 'must be 3 or 4'; Roblox builds use 3). Arithmetic operators work componentwise via VM fast paths (lvmexecute.cpp:1758 vector ADD does scalar vb[i]+vc[i], also SUB/MUL/DIV/UNM). vector library (VM/src/lveclib.cpp): create, magnitude, normalize, cross, dot, angle, floor, ceil, abs, sign, clamp, min, max + vector.zero/vector.one constants. Determinism: f32 component arithmetic is deterministic IF no FMA/fast-math (matches grabby C1) — but magnitude/normalize/angle call sqrtf/transcendentals (libm surface, needs pure-Rust). For grabby, vector is likely DEFERRABLE (galaxy.koto uses [x,y] tables + .cos(), not the vector type).

findings.topic: BUFFER library — strong deterministic byte/int/fixed-point channel
findings.finding: VM/src/lbuflib.cpp: a fixed-size mutable byte array (LUA_TBUFFER GC type, LuauBuffer struct). API: create(size), fromstring, tostring, len, copy, fill, readi8/u8/i16/u16/i32/u32, readf32/f64, write* counterparts, readstring/writestring, readbits/writebits (sub-byte), readinteger/writeinteger (variable 1-8 byte width). CRUCIAL: all multi-byte access is normalized to LITTLE-ENDIAN regardless of host (htole16/32/64 + memcpy, lbuflib.cpp:8 #include<endian.h>, lines 27-31) → byte-portable across x86_64/aarch64/wasm32. readi32/readu32/readinteger give EXACT integer round-trips; readf32/f64 are raw IEEE bit reinterpret. => buffers are an excellent deterministic integer / Q16.16 / serialization channel for rustia, AND a natural fit for the serde bridge. rustia must implement little-endian byte order explicitly (do NOT use host endianness).

bit32 (VM/src/lbitlib.cpp, 15 fns): arshift, band, bnot, bor, bxor, btest, extract, lrotate, lshift, replace, rrotate, rshift, countlz, countrz, byteswap. Operates on uint32 (numbers truncated to 32-bit, modular) — fully deterministic, no libm. utf8 (VM/src/lutf8lib.cpp, 5 fns + utf8.charpattern): offset, codepoint, char, len, codes — deterministic. os (VM/src/loslib.cpp, only 4 fns): clock, date, difftime, time — ALL NONDETERMINISTIC (wall clock); Luau already strips os.execute/getenv/exit/remove/rename/tmpname for sandboxing. => For grabby determinism, rustia must stub/virtualize or remove os.time/os.clock/os.date (or feed a deterministic virtual clock).

VM/src/lmathlib.cpp ~37 entries. EXACT/deterministic with no libm (safe on hardware): abs, ceil, floor, round, sign, clamp, min, max, fmod (use deterministic impl), modf, frexp, ldexp, map, lerp, isnan, isinf, isfinite, deg/rad (x*const), sqrt (IEEE-754 correctly-rounded → safe with hardware sqrt). TRANSCENDENTAL (REQUIRE pure-Rust libm for cross-platform bit-parity, the constraint already in 00-constraints.md): sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, sinh, cosh, tanh, exp, log, log10, pow. SPECIAL: math.noise = Perlin (uses fixed kPerlinHash[257] table + f32 gradients in lmathlib.cpp — replicate the table exactly). math.pi/math.huge are constants. fmod/pow are libm-backed in Luau (fmod, pow) → include in libm port. This is the single biggest correctness-porting burden for bit-exact determinism.

TM enum (VM/src/ltm.h, VM/src/ltm.cpp:38 names): __index, __newindex, __mode, __namecall, __call, __iter, __len, __eq, __add, __sub, __mul, __div, __idiv, __mod, __pow, __unm, __lt, __le, __concat, __type, __metatable (21). __tostring is NOT in the fast TM array — handled separately via luaL_callmeta (laux.cpp:663). NOTABLE DELTAS vs Lua 5.x: (a) NO __gc (Luau has no Lua-level finalizers; userdata use C destructors via lua_newuserdatadtor/tagged dtors). (b) __namecall is Luau-specific (fuses method lookup+call for obj:method()). (c) __iter is Luau-specific (generalized iteration). (d) __type/__metatable customize typeof()/getmetatable. (e) > and >= compile to swapped __lt/__le (no separate metamethods); Luau does NOT synthesize __le from __lt. (f) No __band/__bor/etc (bitwise are bit32 fns, not operators). Raw access: rawget, rawset, rawequal, rawlen, getmetatable, setmetatable all present (lbaselib). Metatable lock via __metatable field (setmetatable errors if present) AND table.freeze/readonly flag (see sandbox).

Two table flags in the LuaTable struct: `readonly` (table.freeze / lua_setreadonly — writes raise luaG_readonlyerror, lapi.cpp:893,998) and `safeenv` (lua_setsafeenv, lapi.cpp:911 — marks globals as un-tampered so the compiler's import fast-paths / builtin FASTCALLs are valid). luaL_sandbox freezes the global table + string metatable and sets safeenv. table.freeze/table.isfrozen/table.clone exposed. Strings have a shared metatable with __index=string (so `('x'):upper()` works). For rustia: implement freeze/readonly (cheap bool on table) and a safeenv concept to license global-builtin specialization; the sandbox (frozen globals) is also what makes N-VM Send+Sync safe to share base library tables.

Globals: pcall, xpcall, error (with level), assert (lbaselib). coroutine (VM/src/lcorolib.cpp, 8 fns): create, resume, running, status, wrap, yield, isyieldable, close (5.4-style close present). Status names: running/suspended/normal/dead (+ a second dead for LUA_COFIN finished, lcorolib.cpp:12). Luau coroutines are FULL stackful coroutines (separate lua_State per coro, ldo.cpp resume/yield via longjmp/protected calls in C++). This is the direct analog of grabby's steppable/yield-resumable requirement: rustia's VM should model each coroutine as an independent resumable execution context with explicit suspend points, and the FUEL budget (C3) should be checked at the interpreter loop / VM_INTERRUPT hook rather than wall-clock. Luau already has an interrupt callback (l_setbit interrupt, used for cooperative cancellation) — rustia's deterministic fuel maps onto exactly this interrupt hook.

NaN as table KEY is rejected ('table index is NaN' error in luaH_set). NaN!=NaN holds (luai_numeq). NaN ordering: all comparisons false. tostring(0/0)→fixed 'nan'/'-nan' and 1/0→'inf'/'-inf' via Schubfach (deterministic), but string.format('%f',nan) via platform snprintf may differ. f64 NaN bit patterns are NOT canonicalized in the value (stored as-is) — a determinism concern only if scripts can produce/observe distinct NaN payloads (rare; arithmetic NaNs from the same ops are reproducible if no FMA). math.isnan/isinf/isfinite provided. rustia must (a) reject NaN keys identically, (b) use the deterministic Schubfach nan/inf strings, (c) avoid platform snprintf for %f.

Weak tables via __mode 'k'/'v' supported (VM/src/lgc.cpp:326-337), cleared in the GC atomic phase. NO Lua-level finalizers (__gc absent), so 'finalizer timing/order' is a NON-issue at the language level — one fewer determinism hazard than Lua 5.4. Remaining hazard: WHEN weak entries get cleared depends on GC cycle timing, which is nondeterministic w.r.t. allocation. => grabby/rustia should avoid game logic that OBSERVES weak-table membership; if weak tables are needed, rustia should either run GC at deterministic fuel boundaries or document that weak-table contents are not part of the deterministic state. Luau GC is incremental tri-color generational; rustia can choose a simpler deterministic collection point.

MINIMUM-VIABLE (needed by galaxy.koto scenarios + console + AI leaves): local/global vars, numeric & generic for, while/repeat, if/elseif/else, functions+closures+varargs, tables/arrays/map literals, indexing, all arithmetic+comparison+concat+logical operators, method calls (a:m()/a.m()), string literals, return/break. Luau-specific niceties that are cheap and likely used: continue, compound assignment (+=,-=,*=,/=,//=,%=,^=,..=), floor division //, number literals (0x,0b,1_000), string interpolation (`{expr}`), generalized iteration (for v in t with __iter), if-then-else EXPRESSIONS. DEFERRABLE: full gradual type-checker (strict/nonstrict/nocheck) — types are ERASED at compile time and carry zero runtime semantics, so a parser that ACCEPTS and IGNORES annotations + generics is enough for runtime compat; the type checker (Analysis/) is a separate ~huge subsystem only needed for editor/diagnostics. Type functions (`type X = ...` user type functions), attributes (@native/@checked), and default args are parse-and-mostly-ignore for an interpreter (no JIT → @native is a no-op; default args need minor desugar support).

Luau removed vs Lua 5.x: goto/labels; _ENV / setfenv-getfenv at language level (replaced by sandbox/safeenv + per-closure env is gone); the __gc finalizer; load/loadstring/dofile/loadfile of arbitrary source at runtime in sandbox (require is the controlled module path); os.execute/io library (no io library at all); collectgarbage is restricted (gcinfo present). integer subtype of Lua 5.3/5.4 (// and bitwise differ — Luau uses bit32, not 5.3 operators). This SHRINKS the surface vs full Lua 5.4. rustia should NOT implement goto, _ENV, io, or Lua-5.4 integer arithmetic semantics.

90 opcodes (LOP_NOP..LOP_CMPPROTO, LOP__COUNT, Common/Bytecode.h:65-455). Register-based, fixed 32-bit instructions + AUX words (32-bit immediates for KS keys, jump targets, FORGLOOP, GETIMPORT). Key families: load (LOADNIL/B/N/K/KX), MOVE, globals/upvals/imports (GETGLOBAL/GETIMPORT/GETUPVAL), table (GET/SETTABLE, GET/SETTABLEKS, GET/SETTABLEN, NEWTABLE, DUPTABLE, SETLIST), calls (CALL, RETURN, NAMECALL, FASTCALL/1/2/2K/3, NATIVECALL), control (JUMP/JUMPBACK/JUMPIF*/JUMPXEQK*), arith (ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/MOD/POW/IDIV + K/RK variants, SUBRK/DIVRK), CONCAT, NOT/MINUS/LENGTH, closures (NEWCLOSURE/DUPCLOSURE/CAPTURE/CLOSEUPVALS), loops (FORNPREP/FORNLOOP, FORGPREP/FORGLOOP/FORGPREP_NEXT/INEXT), COVERAGE, BREAK. ROBLOX-SPECIFIC / DEFERRABLE (~8): GETUDATAKS, SETUDATAKS, NAMECALLUDATA, NEWCLASSMEMBER, CALLFB, CMPPROTO (userdata/class system), NATIVECALL (native codegen). FASTCALL* (5 opcodes) are builtin-dispatch optimizations that can be lowered to ordinary CALL in an MVP. Proto flags LPF_NATIVE_* (Bytecode.h:750) are JIT hints (ignorable). typeinfo bytecode (version 3) is optional metadata for native codegen — ignorable in an interpreter. rustia can (a) write its OWN bytecode (not consume Luau's) since it owns the compiler, OR (b) target LBC_VERSION 7. Owning the compiler is recommended: lets rustia add superinstructions and skip Roblox-specific opcodes. MVP opcode set ≈ 70.

VM/src/lstrlib.cpp: byte, char, find, format, gmatch, gsub, len, lower, match, rep, reverse, sub, upper, split (Luau-added), pack, unpack, packsize. Luau pattern matching is Lua 5.1-style (%a %d %s classes, captures, anchors) — NOT PCRE, deterministic. string.pack/unpack: binary (de)serialization with explicit format specifiers incl endianness control — another deterministic byte channel, but redundant with buffer. string.format float specifiers = platform snprintf hazard (see float formatting finding). string.format %d/%x on non-integer floats raises 'number has no integer representation'. rustia must implement Lua-5.1 pattern engine exactly (gsub/match/find are common in console/scenario scripts) and a deterministic string.pack.

Globals (VM/src/lbaselib.cpp + lualib.h): assert, error, gcinfo, getmetatable, setmetatable, next, newproxy, print, rawequal, rawget, rawlen, rawset, select, tonumber, tostring, type, typeof, ipairs, pairs, pcall, xpcall, unpack, require, _G, _VERSION. typeof() differs from type(): typeof returns the __type metafield or userdata tag name (e.g. 'vector', 'buffer'), type() returns the basic type. pairs() returns (next, t, nil); ipairs stops at first nil. require is the controlled module loader (Require/ dir). No dofile/loadstring/load-from-string in sandbox. rustia must implement type vs typeof distinction and the exact ipairs/pairs/next contract.

FULL latest-Luau runtime surface: ~90 opcodes; 9 stable stdlibs (string 16, table ~17, math ~37, os 4, coroutine 8, bit32 15, utf8 5, buffer ~28 methods, vector ~14) + ~26 globals; 21 fast metamethods + __tostring; experimental (DEFER, FFlag-off): int library (~40 fns, LUA_TINTEGER), user-defined class runtime (LUA_TCLASS/OBJECT + 6 opcodes). GRABBY-MINIMAL Luau-compatible subset (scenarios + console + AI leaves): ~70 opcodes (drop UDATA/class/NATIVECALL; FASTCALL→CALL); globals subset {assert,error,print,type,typeof,tostring,tonumber,pairs,ipairs,next,select,pcall,xpcall,setmetatable,getmetatable,raw*,require}; libs {math (incl libm transcendentals + noise if scenarios use cos/sin — galaxy.koto DOES use a.cos()/a.sin()), table (insert/remove/sort/concat/find/clear/freeze/clone), string (format/find/match/gsub/sub/rep/split + pattern engine), bit32 (if fixed-point in-script), buffer (if used as int channel)}; coroutine (for steppable host integration); os MINIMAL/virtualized. DEFER: full type checker (Analysis/), vector type, utf8, string.pack, int64 lib, class system, native codegen/typeinfo bytecode. MVP libs ≈ 5 (math, table, string, bit32, buffer) + coroutine + base globals.

implications: T1 (f64-vs-fixed-point) is RESOLVED in rustia's favor: Luau's f64-only arithmetic is sufficient for grabby because (a) all script-visible integers stay <2^53 where f64 integer math is exact, and (b) the only overflowing op (Q16.16 64-bit multiply) is already a host fn in grabby. rustia does NOT need a fixed-point primitive in its core Value type for Luau-compat. Keep the host-fn channel; offer the `buffer` library (little-endian, exact int read/write) as the secondary deterministic 64-bit/serialization channel. The experimental int64 lib (LUA_TINTEGER, FFlag-off, library-only, no operators) is a later opt-in, not a compat requirement.

rustia MUST NOT use platform snprintf or std float formatting for string.format %e/%f/%g — reference Luau itself is non-deterministic across platforms here. Implement ONE pure-Rust formatter for all targets. For tostring(number), port Luau's exact Schubfach (lnumprint.cpp) for byte-parity; a generic ryu/grisu will round-trip but won't match Luau byte-for-byte.

rustia's insertion-ordered maps are a STRICTER and MORE portable determinism guarantee than Luau's actual hash-bucket pairs() order. Accept the intentional incompatibility (rustia pairs() order != reference-Luau hash order for string/sparse keys) — document it; array-part (1..n) order matches. grabby already relies on insertion order, so this aligns with grabby, not with stock Luau.

The libm transcendental set {sin,cos,tan,asin,acos,atan,atan2,sinh,cosh,tanh,exp,log,log10,pow,fmod} + math.noise (Perlin) is the largest correctness-porting task for bit-exact cross-platform determinism. Use a single pure-Rust libm (e.g. a vendored/audited port) for ALL targets including the native build — do not call the platform libm even on native, or x86_64 vs aarch64 vs wasm32 will diverge. sqrt is IEEE-correctly-rounded so hardware sqrt is safe.

math.random must be reimplemented as exact PCG32 (multiplier 6364136223846793005, PCG-XSH-RR, ldexp/Lemire range mapping) with a FORCED explicit seed — never Luau's time^clock^pointer default. RNG state is per-VM (global_State), which composes cleanly with the N-independent-VMs Send+Sync model.

table.sort must replicate Luau's exact introsort (median-of-3 + Hoare partition + heapsort fallback at ~1.5log2N) to be bit-identical when comparators produce ties; a different correct sort only matches under a strict total order. Provide the same 'invalid order function' / 'table modified during sorting' guards.

Coroutines map directly to the steppable/yield-resumable VM requirement: model each coroutine as an independent resumable context and check the deterministic FUEL budget at the interpreter interrupt hook (Luau already has a VM interrupt callback) instead of wall-clock. coroutine.close (5.4-style) is expected. This also satisfies C3.

NO __gc finalizers in Luau removes a determinism hazard present in Lua 5.4 — rustia gets simpler. Weak tables (__mode) remain a hazard only if logic observes them; collect at deterministic fuel boundaries or exclude weak-table contents from the deterministic state.

rustia should OWN its compiler and bytecode rather than consuming Luau's LBC v7 — it owns the source→bytecode path anyway, can add superinstructions/copy-and-patch (priority 1 FAST, interpreter-tier since JIT is moot in wasm), and can skip the ~8 Roblox-specific opcodes (UDATA/class/NATIVECALL) and the typeinfo bytecode entirely.

Type annotations carry ZERO runtime semantics (erased at compile time) — rustia's parser must ACCEPT and IGNORE the full type grammar (annotations, generics, type functions, attributes) for runtime Luau-compat; the actual gradual type CHECKER (Luau Analysis/) is a separable, large, deferrable subsystem only needed for editor diagnostics, not for running grabby.
os.time/os.clock/os.date are the only wall-clock nondeterminism in the stdlib (io/os.execute already removed by Luau) — rustia must virtualize or stub them behind a deterministic clock for grabby.

MVP scope to earn 'Luau-compatible for grabby': ~70 opcodes, 5 core libs (math/table/string/bit32/buffer) + coroutine + ~26 base globals + 21 metamethods + Lua-5.1 pattern engine + Schubfach tostring + pure-Rust libm. Full Roblox compat (vector type, utf8, string.pack, int64 lib, class system, native codegen, type checker) is deferrable.
open_questions: Does grabby's console / scenario layer actually call math.sin/cos at runtime on the deterministic path? galaxy.koto uses a.cos()/a.sin() but the header says scenarios run ONCE on the authority and ship DATA (recipe-vs-cake), so scenario transcendentals may not need cross-client bit-parity — only the per-tick AI hot path does. Confirm whether any transcendental runs inside the 50Hz deterministic sim vs only in one-shot authority-side generation; this determines how much of the pure-Rust libm is on the determinism-critical path.

Will grabby keep Q16.16 multiply in host Rust (current design) or move it into script via buffer/bit32? If host-fn, rustia needs no in-script 64-bit integer support at all; if in-script, decide between bit32 (32-bit, may overflow Q16.16 products) vs buffer.readinteger/writeinteger (64-bit, exact) vs adopting the experimental int64 lib.

Exact f64 NaN payload handling: can grabby scripts produce divergent NaN bit patterns observable via buffer.readf64/string.pack? If so rustia may need NaN canonicalization; if scripts never serialize raw NaN bits, it's moot.

Should rustia emit Luau-compatible LBC v7 bytecode (interop with Roblox tooling/luau-compile) or a private bytecode? Owning it is recommended for perf, but if any grabby workflow wants to precompile with the upstream luau compiler, v7 compat matters.

Is the experimental int64 library (LuauIntegerLibrary) on a path to become default-on in a near-future Luau release? If Roblox enables it, 'full latest-Luau compat' will eventually require the ~40-fn int library + LUA_TINTEGER value type wired into eq/typeof. Worth tracking the FFlag's rollout.

Luau's user-defined class runtime (LUA_TCLASS/LUA_TOBJECT, DebugLuauUserDefinedClassesRuntime, 6 new opcodes) is brand-new/experimental in 0.727 — is it a Roblox-internal experiment or a coming language feature? Affects whether rustia must eventually support a class system.

Confirm Luau has no __le-derived-from-__lt fallback (Lua 5.3 had it, 5.4 removed it) — source shows separate TM_LT/TM_LE with > and >= compiled as swapped operands; verify there's no runtime __le synthesis.

result.summary: Deep dive on Luau 0.727 (full C++ source at /tmp/luau_src, dated 2026-06-26, newer than public docs). KEY RESULT on the f64-vs-fixed-point tension (T1): Luau is f64-only at the arithmetic level — all ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/etc opcodes fast-path on ttisnumber(double)+vector only. A real int64 value type (LUA_TINTEGER) and a ~40-fn `int` library DO exist in 0.727 but are FFlag-gated OFF (LuauIntegerLibrary defaults false), library-only (no operators, accessed via int.add/int.mul), and undocumented/experimental — so int64 is a deferrable opt-in carrier, NOT a language-visible integer subtype. f64 is sufficient for grabby because all script-visible integers stay <2^53 (exact) and the one overflowing op (Q16.16 multiply) is already a host fn; the `buffer` library (little-endian, exact typed int read/write) is the natural secondary deterministic integer/serialization channel. DETERMINISM SURFACES enumerated with exact algorithms: pairs() iterates array-part 1..n then HASH-BUCKET (node-slot) order, not insertion order, but with a FIXED unseeded string hash so it's run-stable (rustia's required insertion order is intentionally stricter/incompatible for hash keys — acceptable); math.random is exact PCG32 (mult 6364136223846793005) with a time/pointer default seed that MUST be forced; tostring(number) uses deterministic Schubfach but string.format %e/%f/%g uses PLATFORM snprintf (cross-platform determinism HAZARD — rustia must ship one pure-Rust float formatter); table.sort is unstable introsort (median-of-3 + heapsort fallback) needing exact replication for tie byte-parity; the libm transcendental set (sin/cos/tan/asin/acos/atan/atan2/sinh/cosh/tanh/exp/log/log10/pow/fmod + Perlin math.noise) is the biggest bit-exact-determinism porting burden and must use a single pure-Rust libm on ALL targets (sqrt is IEEE-safe). No __gc finalizers (one fewer hazard than Lua 5.4); weak tables exist via __mode. Metamethods: 21 fast TMs + __tostring, including Luau-specific __namecall/__iter/__type, no __le-from-__lt synthesis. Coroutines (create/resume/yield/wrap/status/close/isyieldable) + the existing VM interrupt hook map directly onto the steppable/fuel-limited VM requirement. Bytecode: 90 opcodes (LBC_VERSION target 7, max 11; typeinfo v3), of which ~8 are Roblox-specific (userdata/class) and 5 FASTCALL* are lowerable; rustia should own its own compiler/bytecode. SCOPE TRIAGE: grabby-minimal Luau-compat ≈ 70 opcodes + 5 core libs (math/table/string/bit32/buffer) + coroutine + ~26 base globals + Lua-5.1 pattern engine + Schubfach tostring; type annotations are runtime-erased so the parser need only accept-and-ignore the type grammar (the gradual type CHECKER is a separable deferrable subsystem). Deferrable to full Roblox compat: vector type, utf8, string.pack, int64 lib, user-defined class runtime (new LUA_TCLASS/TOBJECT + 6 opcodes), native codegen/typeinfo bytecode, the type checker.

findings.topic: DECISIVE: wasm32-unknown-unknown build FAILS — verbatim error
findings.finding: `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` fails on the FIRST C++ source file compiled (Ast/src/Cst.cpp). Verbatim: `luau/Ast/include/Luau/Ast.h:6:10: fatal error: 'iterator' file not found  | 6 | #include <iterator>`. Full failing command: `clang++ --target=wasm32-unknown-unknown -std=c++17 -I .../luau/Ast/include -I .../luau/Common/include -DLUAI_MAXCSTACK=1000000 -DLUA_VECTOR_SIZE=3 -c Cst.cpp`. The blocker is MORE fundamental than setjmp: wasm32-unknown-unknown ships NO libc and NO C++ standard library (no libc++/libstdc++ sysroot), so clang++ cannot find even <iterator>. Luau is C++17 and depends on <vector>, <string>, <iterator>, std containers, and C++ exceptions throughout. It never even reaches the setjmp/longjmp error-handling issue. cc-rs invokes plain clang++ with --target=wasm32-unknown-unknown and no sysroot. This cannot be made to work without an entire C++ sysroot, i.e. emscripten or wasi.

findings.topic: Only working wasm path is emscripten (or wasi) — confirmed by ecosystem
findings.finding: mlua/lua-src/luau-src and multiple independent sources (bytedream litbwraw guide, mlua-rs/lua-src-rs PR #7, luau-src-rs issue #2, Simon Willison's pluau-wasm writeup, Fermyon) all state Lua/Luau wasm support is via wasm32-unknown-emscripten ONLY (and not under JIT). Reason cited: 'Lua relies on libc functions not available in WebAssembly (most notably setjmp for error handling); wasm32-unknown-unknown has no libc implementation at all.' Roblox has no official wasm browser client; community Luau-in-browser builds are emscripten REPL modules. luau-src-rs issue #2 is specifically about getting the emscripten target to compile (a flag bug), confirming emscripten is the intended wasm route.

findings.topic: CRITICAL composition blocker: emscripten module does not compose with wasm-bindgen/Bevy
findings.finding: grabby ships as a Bevy app via wasm32-unknown-unknown + wasm-bindgen (one browser module). wasm32-unknown-emscripten is a DIFFERENT rustc/clang target with a different ABI, its own musl-derived libc, its own malloc/sysroot, and its own JS glue runtime. You cannot link emscripten objects into a wasm32-unknown-unknown cdylib, and you cannot mix the two targets in one crate graph / one wasm module. The realistic emscripten options are both non-starters for grabby: (a) run Luau as a SEPARATE emscripten wasm module in a Web Worker and message-pass — kills the tight per-tick loop (10k agent decisions per 20ms tick), adds serialization + cross-module-call overhead, and breaks the deterministic in-process fuel model; (b) recompile the ENTIRE Bevy/wgpu app to emscripten — not Bevy's supported web target (Bevy targets wasm32-unknown-unknown+wasm-bindgen), would be a massive yak-shave with its own breakage. There is no single-module path.

findings.topic: Determinism retrofit — table iteration order is a hard, invasive blocker
findings.finding: grabby HARD-requires insertion-ordered maps for bit-determinism. Luau tables use a hybrid array+hash representation; pairs()/next() iteration order is NOT insertion-ordered and not a stable cross-version guarantee. koto provides insertion-ordered maps natively; Luau does not. Making Luau iteration deterministic+insertion-ordered means rewriting ltable.cpp / lvm table-iteration — deeply invasive C++ surgery that diverges from upstream permanently.

Luau numbers are f64. Cross-platform bit-determinism (x86_64-linux / aarch64-mac / wasm32) requires a pinned pure-software libm (sin/cos/pow/exp/etc) and disabling FMA contraction (-ffp-contract=off, no fast-math). Stock Luau calls the platform libm (lmathlib.cpp), whose transcendental results differ by ULPs across platforms and across emscripten's musl libm. Retrofit = patch lmathlib.cpp to call a pinned portable libm and enforce fp-contract=off at the C++ build level. Doable but is another fork point you must maintain per Luau release.

findings.topic: Determinism retrofit — fuel metering is the one easy part (but coarse)
findings.finding: Luau has lua_Callbacks.interrupt, called at safepoints (loop back-edges, call/ret, gc), and debugstep for single-step mode; mlua exposes Lua::set_interrupt and the interrupt can request a yield. This gives a workable instruction-fuel/timeout hook and is what Roblox uses for runaway-script containment (luau.org/sandbox, discussions #239/#245). Recursion cap via LUAI_MAXCCALLS/C-stack limit is configurable. CAVEAT: interrupts fire at safepoints, not strictly per-bytecode-instruction, so fuel is coarse-grained (per loop iteration / per call). It is deterministic given identical bytecode (Luau bytecode is deterministic per compiler version), so a back-edge/call counter can be made reproducible — but it is not the fine per-instruction fuel a from-scratch VM gives you for free.

findings.topic: Send/Sync — N-VMs-per-thread model is supported by mlua
findings.finding: mlua Lua is !Send by default; enabling feature='send' adds a Send bound to registered Rust closures/UserData and makes the Lua handle Send (movable across threads). Internally access is guarded by a reentrant mutex; mlua docs explicitly recommend 'one Lua VM per thread, run them in parallel' for true parallelism — which exactly matches grabby's N-owned-VMs-across-a-pool model. RegistryKey is Send+Sync. So the Send story is fine: this is NOT a blocker. (Note: 'send' feature forbids non-Send host callbacks, a minor API constraint, and a raw lua_State is still single-threaded — you move whole VMs, never share one.)

Forking Luau C++ for native-only would deliver a fast, mature, full-compat interpreter on x86_64-linux + aarch64-mac. But: (1) wasm32 is a grabby HARD target (priority #3 + a determinism target), and this path produces nothing for browser/mobile — so it does not satisfy the project; (2) achieving bit-determinism requires forking ltable.cpp (iteration order) AND lmathlib.cpp (libm) AND build-flag control (FMA) — invasive and ongoing; (3) the single biggest reason to use real Luau is free full-Luau-compat (priority #4), but you forfeit upstream-tracking the moment you fork for determinism, since every Luau release would need re-patching. Net: even as a partial/native option it is weak.

In-browser JIT is moot (grabby priority #3 explicitly notes this), so the relevant comparison is Luau's interpreter, which is well-optimized (luau.org/performance) and would comfortably beat the koto baselines (koto-int 5.4us, koto-float 4.0us/decision) on native. But that speed is unreachable on grabby's wasm target via this path. Luau static libs ~1.5MB native; an emscripten wasm Luau REPL module is on the order of a few hundred KB to ~1MB plus emscripten JS glue — separate from and additive to the Bevy wasm-bindgen module, not shared.

implications: For grabby's actual shipping target (wasm32-unknown-unknown + wasm-bindgen + Bevy, one browser module), embedding the real Luau C++ VM is NON-VIABLE. Verbatim hard blocker proven locally: Luau C++ will not compile to wasm32-unknown-unknown at all (no C++ stdlib: 'iterator' file not found on the first source file), and the only working wasm path (emscripten) produces an ABI-incompatible module that cannot be linked into or composed with a wasm-bindgen module — leaving only a separate-Web-Worker design that is incompatible with a deterministic 10k-decisions-per-20ms in-process tick.

This VALIDATES the rustia from-scratch-Rust-interpreter decision rather than obviating it. A pure-Rust VM compiles cleanly to wasm32-unknown-unknown and composes natively into the Bevy/wasm-bindgen module — the exact property Luau-C++ cannot provide.

The determinism HARD constraints (insertion-ordered maps, pinned pure-Rust libm, no FMA) are precisely the things Luau does NOT give you and that require invasive, permanent C++ forking (ltable.cpp + lmathlib.cpp + build flags). Forking destroys the one real advantage of embedding Luau (free upstream full-compat), so embedding-then-forking is close to a worst-of-both-worlds.

Keep from Luau as design references for rustia, not as a dependency: (a) the interrupt-at-safepoints fuel/yield mechanism is a good model — but rustia should do per-instruction deterministic fuel which is strictly better; (b) Luau's bytecode/perf techniques (luau.org/performance) are worth studying; (c) the N-VMs-per-thread Send model mlua uses maps directly onto rustia's Send+Sync-at-VM-granularity requirement.

fork-Luau-C++-for-native-only is at best a stopgap and does not meet grabby (wasm32 is required); do not pursue it as the primary path. If a native-only fast path were ever wanted, mlua+luau+vendored already works out-of-the-box natively (33s build, correct results) — but it inherits all the determinism-retrofit costs above.

Not tested here (wasi target + emscripten not installed; emcc/em++ absent on this machine). Strongly expected to still fail the single-browser-module composition test for the same ABI reasons as emscripten, but the compile step itself would likely get further than wasm32-unknown-unknown.

result.summary: Embedding the real Luau C++ VM compiled to wasm is NON-VIABLE for grabby's actual target and does not obviate rustia. Decisive, locally-reproduced evidence: mlua+Luau (vendored, Luau 0.663) builds and runs fine on native aarch64-mac, but `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` fails on the very first C++ file with a fundamental blocker — `Ast.h:6:10: fatal error: 'iterator' file not found` — because wasm32-unknown-unknown has no C++ standard library/libc at all (this is even earlier than the well-known setjmp problem). The only working wasm path is emscripten (or wasi), which produces a different-ABI module with its own libc/malloc/JS-glue that CANNOT link into or compose with grabby's wasm32-unknown-unknown + wasm-bindgen Bevy module; the only emscripten options are a separate Web Worker (incompatible with a deterministic 10k-decision-per-20ms in-process tick) or recompiling all of Bevy to emscripten (unsupported). On top of that, Luau cannot meet grabby's HARD determinism constraints without an invasive, permanent C++ fork (insertion-ordered table iteration in ltable.cpp, pinned pure-software libm in lmathlib.cpp, FMA/fast-math disabled) — and forking forfeits the one benefit of using real Luau (free upstream full-compat). Send/Sync is fine (mlua `send` feature + one-VM-per-thread matches grabby's model), and Luau's interrupt-at-safepoints hook is a usable but coarse fuel mechanism. fork-Luau-C++-for-native-only is VIABLE-WITH-MAJOR-CAVEATS but fails grabby outright because wasm32 is a required target.

findings.finding: Only SEND is required for the VM; SYNC is required only for shared immutable data (compiled bytecode/LUTs behind Arc), never for the VM's mutable execution state. NO grabby code anywhere shares a single &VM across threads simultaneously. Evidence: (a) the AI bake-off runs strictly single-threaded — benches/bakeoff.rs builds one World + one Selector and calls tick_with on one thread; koto_path.rs holds ONE KotoSelector whose koto: Koto VM is called n times per tick on the same thread, never shared. (b) The real sim App is !Send and is stored as a Bevy NonSend resource that PINS every sim tick to one thread: view/src/lib.rs:68-71 'bevy_app::App is !Send, so a SimHost is stored as a NonSend resource — which also pins every sim tick to one thread'. (c) The console Koto VM is likewise !Send/NonSend: view/src/console.rs:296 'a Koto VM (NonSend: the VM is !Send)' and console.rs:93 insert_non_send(KotoRepl::new()). (d) The only real threads spawned run SEPARATE worlds and communicate by MOVE/message-passing, not shared &VM: net/src/bin/server.rs:59 std::thread::spawn for the tokio accept loop with mpsc channels ('Build the game on the main thread (App is !Send)…Channels between the network (tokio tasks) and the game loop (main thread)'), and view/src/netclient.rs:70/151 std::thread::spawn for the embedded host server (a distinct GameServer/App). No rayon / par_iter / par_iter_mut / thread::scope over VMs exists in sim/src or view/src. The probe ai_bakeoff/tests/koto_probe.rs only asserts KValue: Send+Sync (kvalue_is_send_sync), and the bake-off README states 'KValue: Send+Sync under the arc feature (the N-VMs-across-threads parallel model holds)'. The brief's design model 'N independent VMs across a thread pool' = each VM owned by one thread (work-stealing MOVES owned VMs) → needs Send. Two threads holding &VM concurrently (the only thing that needs Sync) is never done and is not part of the design.

Per-agent persistent state in ai_bakeoff/src/lib.rs World (parallel Vec<...> arrays): inputs [i32;4]=16B; q [i32;6]=24B; trace [i32;6]=24B; last_action u8=1B; mood i32=4B; neighbors [u32;4]=16B; mood_prev (scratch) i32=4B. Sum ≈ 89 B/agent. The MUTABLE state a rollback/snapshot must capture = inputs(16)+q(24)+trace(24)+last_action(1)+mood(4) ≈ 69 B/agent (neighbors are static, not captured). state_hash() hashes a 53 B/agent subset (q+trace+last_action+mood). At 4000 agents: hot working set ≈ 356 KB; one snapshot frame ≈ 276 KB. IMPORTANT: the lib.rs comment flags this per-agent Q-table as a deliberate stress test — 'Per-agent here to stress storage; real design shares one table per crew-TYPE + a per-agent offset (§2.2)', so production per-agent learned state is much smaller (≈ inputs+last_action+mood+offset, ~tens of bytes).

findings.topic: Snapshot / rollback ring multiplier for AI state
findings.finding: If AI state runs inside the deterministic sim it must ride the rollback ring. Ring depth = 24 frames: sim/src/predict/wire.rs:29 'pub const CLIENT_RING_DEPTH: usize = 24'; INPUT_REDUNDANCY=5 (wire.rs:23), ONE_WAY_TICKS=5 (wire.rs:18). The ring is IN-MEMORY plain typed structs, NO serde (sim/src/snapshot.rs:9). So per-agent captured AI state is multiplied ×24: at 4000 agents and ~69 B/agent that is ≈ 6.6 MB of AI rollback state; with the production shared-Q-table design it drops to well under 1 MB. Capture/restore budget target: snapshot.rs:6 'restore ≤ 1 ms at M1 scale (half the ~2 ms rollback slice)'. Note: today's sim has NO learned/RL per-agent state captured — the AI kernel (SARSA/IAUS/eligibility) does NOT yet exist in sim/src; only the bake-off spike has it. The live NPC brain (sim/src/brain.rs, crew.rs, npc_farm.rs) is stateless integer utility selection re-derived each tick (NavGoal is capture-free), so adding learned AI state is NET-NEW snapshot payload.

findings.topic: Koto VM RSS at scale — not derivable
findings.finding: NOT derivable from source. The bake-off uses exactly ONE Koto VM shared across all agents (KotoSelector::new() called once in benches/bakeoff.rs; koto.call_function looped over agents), so VM count scales with THREADS, not agents. No RSS instrumentation exists. The bake-off README explicitly lists 'Koto VM RSS / iOS-device / browser-wasm memory' as DEFERRED + still-open. Treat koto per-VM RSS as a must-measure unknown; rustia should target a small fixed per-VM overhead since the design wants N VMs across a thread pool.

Confirmed: the modeled hot path calls a script function ONCE PER AGENT PER TICK. ai_bakeoff/src/lib.rs World::tick_with loops 'for i in 0..self.n { … let action = sel.select(&self.luts, &inputs, last, &mut rng); … }' and KotoSelector::select (ai_bakeoff/src/koto_path.rs) does 'self.koto.call_function(self.argmax.clone(), &args)' with 5 scalar KValue args, once per call. README finding #2: 'A Koto call per agent per tick does NOT scale — ~30-40× the floor … eats the entire 20ms tick by ~3700/5000 agents.' This is THE finding motivating a batched decide-N-agents-per-VM-call API for rustia: per-call marshalling + VM entry dominates. (The real sim does not yet do per-agent script calls — brain is native Rust; the console VM calls koto only on REPL input via call_function in view/src/console.rs.)

Both are real; CANONICAL headline per-decision = 5.4 µs (koto-int float-free). The README table's 6.40 ms @ 1k = 6.40 µs/decision is the SMALL-N datapoint inflated by per-tick fixed overhead (contagion snapshot pass, cache warm-up) amortized over only 1000 agents. The per-decision figure is taken from the larger, amortized runs: 10.82 ms/2000 = 5.41 µs and 27.18 ms/5000 = 5.436 µs — both ≈5.4 µs, the steady-state per-agent cost once fixed per-tick costs wash out. So 5.4 µs is canonical (representative scaled per-decision); 6.4 µs@1k is the raw low-N point. (koto-float steady: 19.99 ms/5000 = 4.0 µs = the canonical 4.0 µs.) Golden AI hash 0x31c6ec2734ea6fa2 is produced bit-identically by BOTH native and koto-int (float-free), proving determinism-equivalence.

implications: VM type must be Send (own-and-move across a thread pool); it does NOT need to be Sync — do not pay for interior synchronization on the VM's mutable state. Make only the shared immutable artifacts (compiled bytecode/chunk, LUT/const pools, string interner) Sync via Arc so all per-thread VMs share one read-only copy. This matches grabby's actual usage (single-thread-pinned VMs, separate-world threads via channels) and the 'N independent VMs across a thread pool' design — Sync-at-VM-granularity is over-engineering grabby never exercises.

Design a batched decide-N-agents-per-VM-call API. The dominant cost is per-call VM entry + arg marshalling at one call per agent per tick (5.4 µs/decision, ~39× native, fatal above ~900-3700 agents at 50 Hz). A single VM call that decides a batch of agents (passing columnar arrays in, action array out) amortizes entry/marshalling and is the lever that makes scripted AI viable at thousands of agents.

Per-agent learned AI state is small in absolute terms (~69 B mutable/agent stress-case, far less with a shared per-crew-type Q-table), but the 24-deep rollback ring multiplies it ~24× (~6.6 MB worst-case at 4000 agents). rustia/GC must make per-agent AI state cheap to snapshot+restore (plain POD, no serde, ≤1 ms restore). Favor a flat, columnar, copy-snapshotable representation over GC-traced per-agent objects; learned state should live in host-side Rust arrays, not script-heap objects, so it rides the existing in-memory typed ring.

Keep the hot per-agent inner math in Rust-native fixed-point (it is effectively free: 10k agents in 1.43 ms, 14× under budget). Reserve the script VM for coarse/infrequent leaves (a few Hz, per-action-change) and console/content. This bounds how fast the interpreter core must be: it does NOT need to win the inner per-agent loop, it needs low call-entry overhead and a batch API.

Memory priority #2 denominator: per VM, target a small fixed RSS (since VM count = thread count, not agent count). The per-agent denominator for AI state is ~tens of bytes (shared Q-table design) to ~89 B (per-agent stress), ×24 for rollback — plan the allocator/GC so this is contiguous and snapshot-friendly.

Determinism is already proven achievable with Q16.16 + libm-built LUTs + host integer helpers producing a bit-identical cross-arch hash (0x31c6...). rustia should expose first-class integer/shift/bitwise ops (Koto lacks >>, //, bitwise; / promotes to f64) so scripts can do fixed-point without a host-call tax — but note finding #3 of the README: forking for integer ops would NOT rescue per-tick-per-agent perf (the cost is the interpreted VM, ~4 µs even with zero host calls).

result.verdict: GO. The MVP claim HOLDS — and is exceeded — on the REAL arithmetic-bound integer-AI kernel, not just the string-sort bench. Apples-to-apples (only the IAUS argmax in script, identical to grabby's koto path): reference Luau = 0.73 us/decision vs koto-int 5.9 / koto-float 4.4 on the SAME machine => 8.1x / 6.0x faster, comfortably under the 1.0-1.25 us/decision target. Even the pessimistic case where the ENTIRE loop (select+SARSA+contagion) runs inside the interpreter is 1.45 us/decision = 4.1x over koto-int (slightly over the 1.25 absolute target but the 4x multiplier holds). FFI entry is a non-issue (0.030 us/call, ~4% of cost) — like koto, the cost is VM execution, but Luau's register VM executes this kernel ~6-8x cheaper than koto's. Budget impact: at 5 ms, Luau realistic seats ~6850 agents vs koto's ~850 — the "thousands @ 50 Hz" that killed koto is reachable with a Luau-class VM. CAVEAT for design: this measures REFERENCE Luau (mlua/luau709) as the performance TARGET/proxy; rustia is a from-scratch VM and must hit this bar, it does not automatically inherit it. Also note koto-int was SLOWER than koto-float purely because koto lacks >>/integer-div and needs host fxmul/curve calls; rustia, built from scratch with native integer/fixed-point ops, can run the determinism-safe Q16.16 path WITHOUT that host-call tax, so the float-vs-int gap that hurt koto need not apply.
caveats: PERF PROXY, NOT determinism path: the considerations use f64 Luau math (Luau numbers are doubles), matching grabby's kotof proxy for a fair comparison. The HARD determinism constraint (Q16.16, no-FMA, pure libm, bit-identical x86/arm/wasm) is NOT exercised here. A determinism-safe Luau-side fixed-point path (f64 + floor/bit32, or host integer helpers, or rustia native integer ops) must be measured separately; it could be slower (koto-int was 1.35x slower than koto-float for exactly this reason).

This is REFERENCE Luau (mlua, luau0-src luau709) — NOT rustia. It establishes the performance bar the from-scratch rustia VM must reach; rustia's actual us/decision is unmeasured and TBD. The number validates the LANGUAGE/bytecode-VM approach beats koto ~6-8x on this kernel, not that any specific rustia implementation will.

Curve approximation: the float path uses x*x for kind 0 instead of the native logistic LUT (identical to grabby's kotof). The real determinism path's logistic would be a LUT lookup (host call ~0.03 us, or in-VM table) — negligible add, but the exact curve differs.
aarch64-mac, single-threaded ONLY. wasm32-unknown-unknown perf (priority #3, browser/mobile) is NOT measured — Luau-in-wasm under an interpreter could differ materially. No x86_64-linux number.

VM-INTERNAL uses 1-based flat Luau tables; table indexing has overhead a register/local-heavy port could cut, so 1.45 us is a conservative upper bound for fully-scripted. It also runs MORE work in-script than koto did (koto kept SARSA+contagion in Rust), so it is NOT directly comparable to the koto numbers — only the REALISTIC path is apples-to-apples with koto.

Timing via std::time::Instant with warmup, not Criterion; no confidence intervals. Mitigated by large n*ticks and cross-run stability (two runs within ~3%) and native matching grabby's number to 3 sig figs.

result.verdict: GO. The feared ~4x wasm dispatch tax is decisively refuted. For the match/br_table dispatch (the style we should ship), wasm-in-V8 runs at 0.85x-1.10x of native ns/dispatch - i.e. essentially parity, with node V8 actually FASTER than the native build. So the dispatch loop itself imposes ~zero wasm penalty: whatever per-decision cost rustia achieves natively, in-browser it is ~1.0-1.3x of that, dominated by the interpreter's native instruction count, not by any wasm dispatch tax. The browser viability question therefore reduces to the native per-decision cost (a later spike), and the wasm-tax GATE is GO. Second finding answers the target-split-dispatch question: NO split needed. Function-pointer/call-threading is WORSE on BOTH targets - 1.84x slower than match on native, and it also carries a higher wasm tax (1.34-1.51x, since call_indirect adds table bounds + type checks). The portable match/br_table is optimal on native AND wasm; computed-goto/tail-threading is unnecessary for V8 because plain br_table is already at native parity. Ship one dispatch style (big match), everywhere.
caveats: Measured only on aarch64-apple-darwin host (V8 via node/deno on ARM mac). x86_64-linux and mobile-ARM V8 may show different absolute numbers and a different tax ratio - the ~1.0x parity is the aarch64 finding, not yet proven on the other two HARD-CONSTRAINT targets.
wasmtime/Cranelift NOT measured (not installed; skipped per instructions to avoid ratholing). In-browser product is V8/SpiderMonkey/JSC anyway, but the non-browser wasm path is unmeasured.

Microbenchmark of pure dispatch + integer/fixed-point ALU only. A real Luau VM adds heap loads/stores, table/string ops, GC, and closure calls; wasm linear-memory bounds checks and call_indirect for host/closure calls could stress wasm differently than this register-only loop. The ~1.0x tax applies to the dispatch+ALU core, not the whole interpreter.
Does not measure absolute rustia per-decision cost vs the grabby <=5ms/tick budget - that needs the full VM. This spike only proves the wasm/native RATIO for dispatch.
